findings.title: Failed run leaves a partial output directory that blocks all reruns
findings.message: Every step after output.mkdir (extract_verified, new-app.py exit code, the Title sentinel check) can fail and leave a half-populated output directory behind. Because mkdir is deliberately exclusive, rerunning the same command then dies with FileExistsError, and the leftover directory can be mistaken for a successfully generated consumer. Generation should be all-or-nothing.
findings.evidence:
output.mkdir(mode=0o700)  # exclusive; never replace existing source or notebooks
    sdk = checker.extract_verified(args.sdk, output/'sdk', verified)
    app = output/'Work Log'
    subprocess.run([sys.executable, '-B', str(sdk/'scripts/new-app.py'), str(app),
                    '--module=example.com/vellum-work-log', '--template=document'], check=True)

findings.title: scripts/ dir inserted at sys.path[0] can shadow stdlib modules
findings.message: The checker is loaded by explicit file location (spec_from_file_location), so this module-level insert is not needed for that import; its only effect is that scripts/ is searched before the standard library for everything imported afterwards, including inside exec_module(checker). A scripts/types.py or scripts/json.py would silently shadow the stdlib.
findings.suggestion:
Append instead of inserting at position 0 so stdlib and site-packages win, and verify whether the entry is needed at all:

sys.path.append(str(ROOT / 'scripts'))

findings.title: Path.is_relative_to requires Python 3.9, raising AttributeError on older interpreters
findings.message: Path.is_relative_to was added in Python 3.9, and it is the newest API used in this file (everything else is 3.5-era). On an older interpreter the containment guard raises AttributeError after verify_archive has already done its work, so the script crashes with an unrelated traceback instead of the intended error. If the project still supports pre-3.9, use an equivalent comparison.

fix.before:
if output.is_relative_to(ROOT):
        raise ValueError('output must be outside the checkout')
fix.after:
if output == ROOT or ROOT in output.parents:
        raise ValueError('output must be outside the checkout')

findings.title: Nested --output paths fail with a cryptic FileNotFoundError
findings.message: mkdir() defaults to parents=False, so an --output like ~/.local/share/worklogs/run1 fails with a bare FileNotFoundError ('No such file or directory') naming the parent, which reads like a bug in the script rather than a usage problem.
findings.suggestion: Pass parents=True (intermediate directories get umask-default permissions; only the leaf is 0700), or catch FileNotFoundError and print an actionable message telling the user to create the parent first.
findings.evidence: output.mkdir(mode=0o700)  # exclusive; never replace existing source or notebooks

fix.before: output.mkdir(mode=0o700)  # exclusive; never replace existing source or notebooks
fix.after: output.mkdir(mode=0o700, parents=True)  # exclusive; never replace existing source or notebooks

findings.title: Child process stdout pollutes the script's machine-readable output contract
findings.message: The script's only deliberate stdout line is print(app), i.e. the created application path, which suggests piping into a follow-up build step. new-app.py inherits stdout, so any progress or log output it prints is mixed into that stream and breaks naive consumers like "create.py ... | xargs go build".
findings.suggestion: Discard (or capture) the child's stdout while leaving stderr intact so check=True failures still surface, e.g. add stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL to the subprocess.run call.
